title: Frequently Asked Questions
heroSubheading: Quick answers to common questions about admissions, portals, and payments.

items.heading: What are the minimum requirements for undergraduate admission?

children.text: Five O'level credits including English Language and Mathematics in not more than two sittings, plus a minimum UTME score of 140 (subject to change based on national policy), a relevant subject combination for your chosen course, and successful completion of Post-UTME screening.

items.heading: Can I apply through Direct Entry?

children.text: Yes. Direct Entry candidates need an NCE (minimum merit pass), OND (minimum upper credit), or A'level passes in relevant subjects, plus five O'level credits including English and Mathematics, and successful completion of Direct Entry screening.

items.heading: Do I need to select TSU as my first choice on JAMB?

children.text: You must select Taraba State University as either your first or second choice institution on your UTME form.

items.heading: What documents do I need for admission?

children.text: Original and photocopy of your O'level result(s), birth certificate or declaration of age, local government certificate of origin, recent passport photographs (8 copies), JAMB result slip, and A'level/NCE/OND result if applying through Direct Entry.

items.heading: What do I need for a Postgraduate Diploma (PGD)?

children.text: A Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognized university, with a minimum of Third Class degree or HND (Lower Credit).

items.heading: What are the requirements for a Master's degree?

children.text: A Bachelor's degree with at least Second Class Lower division, or a PGD with a minimum of Upper Credit if you don't have a directly relevant first degree, plus your NYSC discharge or exemption certificate.

items.heading: What do I need to apply for a PhD?

children.text: A Master's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.5 on a 5-point scale, a research proposal in your intended area of study, and satisfactory performance in the entrance examination or interview.

items.heading: How do I start an application?

children.text: Visit apply.tsuniversity.edu.ng for undergraduate, sandwich, or diploma applications, or pgapp.tsuniversity.edu.ng for postgraduate applications. Full links for every portal are on our Portals page.

items.heading: I forgot my portal password — what do I do?

children.text: Use the password reset option on your specific portal's login page. If that doesn't work, contact the ICT Help Desk at helpdesk.tsuniversity.ng.

items.heading: Which portal do I use to check my results?

children.text: Use the Student Result Checker at resultchecker.tsuniversity.edu.ng.

items.heading: Where do I make payments for fees or applications?

children.text: All payments are made through the official Payments portal at payments.tsuniversity.edu.ng. Do not pay through any other channel or third party.

(Sample answer — to be confirmed with the Bursary/Admissions office) Application fees are generally non-refundable once submitted, including in cases where an application is unsuccessful. Please confirm the current policy with the Admissions office before paying.
(Sample answer — to be confirmed) Payments are typically accepted via debit card and bank transfer through the secure payment gateway on the Payments portal.

items.heading: How can I contact the university?

children.text: You can reach us at registrar@tsuniversity.edu.ng, or through the Contact page on this website.

items.heading: Where can I find important academic dates?

children.text: Visit our Academic Calendar page for resumption dates, registration windows, examination periods, and other key dates for the current session.

items.heading: I have a technical issue with the website or a portal — who do I contact?

children.text: For website or portal issues, contact the ICT Help Desk at helpdesk.tsuniversity.ng.
